column4: Night on an open desert plain. A small campfire on the ground throws his shadow huge and doubled across the ground toward us. He stands still beside the fire, seen from behind and a little to the side; his medium wolfdog sits at the left.
Side-on view at night. The campfire's flames lean and reach toward him as if calling him; his long shadows sprawl across the ground to the right. He stands holding the Les Paul.
A high crane shot looking down over the night plain. Rings of light ripple outward from the small campfire across the ground; he stands near the fire, small in the frame.
Low angle at night. He plays the Les Paul beside the campfire, hunched over the guitar; ribbons of smoke rise from the fire and sway in the air beside him.
The widest shot: a vast night sky full of stars and the Milky Way above a flat plain; the campfire and his figure are tiny at the bottom of the frame.
The campfire leaps high; a serpent made of smoke rises out of the flames and turns its head toward him. He stands beside the fire with the Les Paul.
A close-up from the chest up, three-quarter view, as he sings: the string veil hides his whole face. The smoke serpent's head hangs over his shoulder, looking down at him. Starry night behind.
A wide two-shot at night: the smoke serpent arches out of the campfire over him and breathes smoke down over him. He stands looking up at it.
Ground-level wide shot: the smoke serpent pours down into rivers of smoke that flow across the plain past him.
The night sky catches fire from the horizon upward; he stands small on the plain beside the campfire, silhouetted against the burning sky.
Seen from behind, he stands on the plain looking up: in the burning sky, ancient rock-art glyphs (an antlered stick figure, a spiral, a handprint) glow like constellations made of stars.
Storm clouds roll in and break the burning sky apart above the plain; he is a small silhouette below.
